Before using A/B testing for experiments, you need to clarify the experimental scene and plan the event tracking data access plan required for the experiment, and the R & D engineer completes the data access landing according to the data access plan. The Growth Marketing Suite SDK is a self\-developed event tracking tool for basic data collection and analysis. This article introduces you to data access capabilities and general access processes.

* **SDK Release Log:**  See [SDK Update Log ](https://www.volcengine.com/docs/6285/69616)for details.

* **SDK developer:**  Beijing BytePlus Technology Co., Ltd.

* **Key Features:**  The Growth Marketing Suite SDK supports the collection of fundamental data for the analysis of statistical metrics such as new additions, activations, retention, and performance of applications.

<span id="75e4dee9"></span>
# Data flow description

Before data access, you need to have a general understanding of the type and flow of data collected before and after data collection.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

Of which:


* Behavioral data: that is, the data collection scheme formulated according to the analysis business goals, event tracking is carried out at the corresponding location, and when the user triggers a key event, the event tracking report will be sent to the background.

* User data: collected user ID\-related data used to uniquely identify users, as well as user characteristics\-related data required for post\-business analysis.

* Device data: ID data collected to uniquely identify the device, as well as data related to device characteristics required for post\-business analysis.

<span id="59826f20"></span>
# Preparation and access precautions


1. Preparation for work.

   1. Verify that the administrator has completed operations such as creating a group, accessing the DataTester experimental application, etc.

   2. Log in to the DataTester console to obtain information such as the application ID required for subsequent data access.

2. Learn about access considerations.

   * According to the data access scheme, it is clear that the events and their attributes that need to be collected and reported in the future, and whether the list of preset events and attributes meets the business requirements. Please refer to the details of preset events and attributes [Preset Property Summary](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataTester/Preset-Property-Summary).

   * If you need a custom event, you need to know the data format requirements for the corresponding event and its properties, see [Supported Data Formats (Custom Events/Properties)](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataTester/Supported-Data-Formats-Custom-Events-Properties).

      <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="2">warning      </div>
      

      <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="2">If the data format does not comply with the specification, it may cause the data access operation to be normal, but the data reported later is empty or abnormal, so you need to pay attention to the data format requirements, such as defining the attribute of the numeric type and the data type as string.      </div>
      

   * According to the data access scheme, understand the type of user identification supported during data access, and unify the statistical caliber. Please refer to the details [Supported User Unique Identifiers](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataTester/Supported-User-Unique-Identifiers).

<span id="aa0b4a06"></span>
# Data Reporting & Caching Policy

<span id="1dccfc2f"></span>
## Data reporting strategy


|**SDK** |**Reporting policy description** |**Is it configurable?**  |**Can it be automatically adjusted according to the network environment?**  |**Can it be reported in time periods?**  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Android |* When the SDK is not initialized, if there are events triggered (including preset and custom), it will be cached in the client side memory, up to 300 caches.<br><br>* After the SDK is initialized, if there is an event triggered (including preset and custom), whether init is called, after init (automatically start after default init) will drop the library, and it will be reported every 60s after starting (up to 1600 items each time, if more than 1600 items are generated in one minute, you need to wait for the next 60s to report).<br><br>* After the SDK is initialized, if you switch users, report it immediately. |No<br><br>Trigger the reporting task every 60 seconds, each request packs 200 event tracking, Android reports up to 8 consecutive requests per task, iOS reports up to 10 consecutive requests per task |No |No |
|iOS |* The SDK is not initialized and will not be cached locally.<br><br>* After the SDK is initialized, if there is an event triggered (including preset and custom), whether init is called, after init (automatically start after default init) will drop the library, and it will be reported every 60s after starting (up to 2000 items each time, if more than 2000 items are generated in one minute, you need to wait for the next 60s to report).<br><br>* After the SDK is initialized, if you switch users, report it immediately. |No |No |No |
|Web JS |Real\-time reporting, but there is an asynchronous queue waiting time of about 30ms. If the number of events triggered within 30ms is less than 20, they will be combined into one report. If there are more than 20 events, they will be reported separately in groups of 20. max_report can set the number of bars. |Configurable maximum number of reports and asynchronous queue wait time:<br><br>max_report: 10 (the number of combined reports defaults to 10)<br><br>reportTime: 30 (Time interval for event reporting to asynchronous queue, default 30ms) |No |No |
|Mini Program<br><br>(WeChat/Byte/Alipay/Baidu/QQ, etc.) |Default real\-time reporting.<br><br><br>* 1.X version: Support to open enable_storage. After opening, it will be reported by default every 5 seconds and up to 5 pieces each time.<br><br>* Version 2.5 and above: Support enable_buffer (buffering), enable_cache (caching).<br><br>   Buffer words:<br><br>   * buffer_interval: Default 5 seconds, can be adjusted<br><br>   * buffer_number: Default 5, can be adjusted |Configurable whether to turn on, number of seconds per interval, and threshold number of times per session<br><br>Only 2.5.0 and above versions support:<br><br><br>* enable_buffer: true//open buffer<br><br>* buffer_interval: 5000//buffer interval, in milliseconds, the default value is 5000<br><br>* buffer_number: 5//Maximum number of buffers, default 5<br><br>* enable_cache: true//open cache |No |No |
|Mini game<br><br>(WeChat/ByteDance/Quick Games, etc.) |Mini Program ||||
|Quick application |Mini Program ||||


<span id="13bf50e4"></span>
## Data caching strategy


|**SDK** |**Data processing mechanism after network abnormalities, crashes, etc. cause failure to report** |**Whether to compress** |**Compression algorithm** |**Is the algorithm customizable?**  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Android |The event tracking package will store db (the event tracking generated before the sdk is initialized will not store db, up to 300 items will be cached; the db will not be stored until initialization. As long as the event tracking cached before the process is not killed will fall into the library), the successful report will be deleted from db, and the failure to report will not be deleted from db. It will not be deleted until the 10\-day expiration date. The db storage amount follows the mobile phone storage space. |Yes |AES encryption + gzip compression |Yes (AES + CBC is supported by default, which needs to be matched with the server side) |
|iOS |The event tracking package will store the SQLite3 database. If the report is successful, it will be deleted from the database. If the report fails, it will not be deleted from db. iOS will not delete local data. SDK has no storage limit, and db storage follows the hard disk size limit of the mobile phone. |Yes |AES encryption + gzip compression |Yes (AES + CBC is supported by default, which needs to be matched with the<br><br><span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/08d82382aa2b4007aa184801858e0d9b~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span><br><br>) |
|Mini Program |Default reporting fails, in the case of enabling cache (1.x version parameters enable_storage, 2.5 and above parameters enable_cache), it will be put into the local storage and wait for the next supplementary reporting (a single key allows storage of the maximum data length of 1MB, all data storage limit is 10MB). |No |without |without |
|Web |Default no mechanism, can be configured to turn on the global<br><br>Use enable_storage: true to enable global configuration. Data that fails to report when the network is abnormal will be stored in localstorage. The next time you visit the page, the data in localstorage will be checked first, and if any, it will be sent. (The number of cache limits does not exceed 50 by default, you can use the storage_num parameter to configure the number of limits). |No |without |without |
